chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, Abu Yazeed, from Ibn Abu Shayba al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Death, death! Indeed, death is inevitable. Death comes with what is in it; it comes with coolness, rest, and the blessed return to the High Paradise for the people of the Abode of Eternity, whose striving was for it and whose desire was in it. And Death comes with what is in it with misery, regret, and the losing return to the Blazing Fire for the people of the Abode of Deception, whose striving was for it and whose desire was in it.'

Then he said, and he (the Prophet) said: 'When the Guardianship of Allah and Happiness are deserved, the Term (of death) comes between the eyes, and Ambition goes behind the back. And when the Guardianship of Satan and Misfortune are deserved, Ambition comes between the eyes, and the Term goes behind the back.'

He said: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, 'Which of the Believers is the most astute?' So he said: 'The one who remembers death the most, and the one who is most prepared for it.'
ai.seo_question: What distinguishes the death of the righteous from the wicked according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the dual nature of death as a transition point, contrasting the 'blessed return' for the righteous with the 'losing return' for the deceitful. It introduces a profound psychological insight: the righteous experience death as a visible reality while worldly hopes fade, whereas the wicked are distracted by fleeting ambitions until death strikes unexpectedly. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *dhikr al-mawt* (remembrance of death) as the key metric for spiritual intelligence (*aklas*), urging believers to prioritize the eternal over the temporal.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Ibn Muskan, from Dawod Bin Farqad Abu Yazeed, from Ibn Abu Shayba Al Zuhry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The death! The death! Indeed, and the death is inevitable. The death comes with what is in it. It comes with the cool breeze and the rest, and the Blessed delight to the Lofty Paradise for the people of the eternal abode which they were striving for, and therein was their interest. And the death come with what is in it with the misery, and the regret, and with the turning to the loss to the Blazing Fire for the people of the house of deception which they were striving for, and therein was their interest.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And he<sup>saww</sup> said:
‘To those who deserve Wilayah (Guardianship) and the Protection of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Salvation, the death comes as it is in front of the eyes and the worldly ambitions are kept backward; but if one is under the wilayah (guardianship) of Satan, in his case misfortune and worldly ambitions come before his eyes, and the reality of the death is kept backward’.

And He<sup>asws</sup> (the Imam<sup>asws</sup>) said that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was asked, ‘Which one of the Believers is the most intelligent?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who most frequently remembers the death, and the one who is most intense in preparing for it’.
en.sarwar: 27. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from ibn Muskan from Dawud ibn Farqad (abu Yazid) from ibn abu Shaybah al-Dhuhriy who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “

(I remind you about) death, (I remind you about) death! Indeed death is inevitable. Death comes along with certain things:It comes with happiness, comfort and the blessed turn to lofty paradise, prepared for the people of eternity, for which they had worked assiduously, with great interest. Death comes along with certain things. It comes with misfortune, regret, with a turn to loss and extremely hot fire, which is prepared for the dwellers of deceitful abode which they had been seeking with great interest.”

The Messenger of Allah then said, “To those who deserve guardianship and protection of Allah and salvation, death seems as if it is before their eyes. The worldly ambitions are kept backward, but if one is under the guardianship of Satan, in his case misfortune and worldly ambitions come before his eyes, and the reality of death is kept backward.’

The Imam then said, ‘The Messenger of Allah was asked, “Who is the most intelligent believer?” He replied, “Those who think about death very often and are very serious to prepare themselves for death.’””
